summary: Turn GIS and earth-observation evidence into prioritised adaptation projects and funder-ready concept notes. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Climate adaptation finance training shows practitioners how to turn spatial climate-risk evidence into prioritised projects and funder-ready proposals. For climate practitioners, GIS officers, and project developers, it covers QGIS-based risk screening and spatial prioritisation, adaptation indicators, and cost-benefit assumptions. Exercises use GIS layers, satellite imagery, and spreadsheet analysis to build a project pipeline and draft a concept note; AI-assisted land-cover classification is covered conceptually.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who translate climate and spatial evidence into adaptation decisions, investment priorities, and funder submissions across water, agriculture, municipalities, conservation, and infrastructure.
modules: Adaptation Indicators and Theory of Change
GCF Concept Notes for Adaptation Finance
prerequisites: Prior work exposure in climate adaptation, GIS, water, agriculture, municipal planning, conservation, infrastructure, or project development is recommended. Basic spreadsheet use is helpful. Coding is not required, and advanced climate modelling is not a prerequisite. Bring a laptop if available; QGIS is a free, open-source option, while Excel access may require a commercial licence.
